Bill.BriefDescription: Notifying tribes of significant natural resource-related action by certain state entities.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to providing notification of natural resourcerelated actions; adding a new section to chapter 43.17 RCW; adding anew section to chapter 43.30 RCW; adding a new section to chapter43.300 RCW; adding a new section to chapter 43.23 RCW; adding a newsection to chapter 43.21A RCW; adding a new section to chapter 47.01RCW; adding a new section to chapter 43.20 RCW; adding a new section tochapter 43.70 RCW; adding a new section to chapter 76.09 RCW; adding anew section to chapter 89.08 RCW; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that open andtransparent governmenttogovernment communication with the federallyrecognized Indian tribes located within the borders of Washingtonshould be encouraged. The legislature further finds that there aremultiple state agencies that manage, regulate, and administer thestate's natural resources. Therefore, those agencies that areresponsible for the state's natural resources should foster governmenttogovernment communications with Indian tribes when natural resourcesare significantly affected by the actions of an agency.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 43.17 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Timely notification of any significant natural resourcerelatedaction undertaken by any state entity listed in subsection (2) of thissection must be provided to the legislative authority of any federallyrecognized Indian tribe when the agency determines that the actionaffects, or could affect, a particular Indian tribe or tribes. (2) This section applies only to the following state entities: (a) The board of natural resources and the department of naturalresources; (b) The forest practices board; (c) The department of fish and wildlife and the fish and wildlifecommission; (d) The department of agriculture; (e) The department of ecology; (f) The state conservation commission; (g) The department of transportation; and (h) The state board of health and the department of health. (3) As used in this section, the term "natural resourcerelatedaction" includes any agency rule, policy statement, order,administrative decision, or execution of statutory functions that isdetermined by the agency to significantly affect, or relate to, thestate's water, mineral, forest, fisheries, or wildlife resources. (4) An agency may satisfy the requirements of this section byproviding electronic notification, or another method of notificationfound by the agency to be most costeffective, to the legislativeauthority of a federally recognized Indian tribe that the agencydetermines would be affected by a natural resourcerelated action. (5) Nothing in this section affects or replaces any othernotification requirement contained in state law. (6) No action may be invalidated based on the failure of an agencyto provide notification to an Indian tribe under this section.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 43.30 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Any rule, policy statement, order, administrative decision, orexecution of statutory functions performed by the department or board SHB 2497 p. 2 must comply with the tribal notification requirements of section 2 ofthis act.
